A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InfoReasoner and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Material moved between the main text and appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original seven-benchmark QA evaluations, reward and search-turn ablations, training dynamics, and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds InfoReasoner evaluations on MATH500 and WebDetective, plus training-cost measurements. The separately attributed frontier-model scores do not affect this assessment.

M1.justification: The gold-class log-probability reward already appears in v1 Equation (17) and Algorithm 1. v3 distinguishes it explicitly from entropy reduction, but semantic clustering, reward combination, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. The added benchmark evaluations do not specify a new algorithmic adaptation.

E1.justification: v3 retains the seven QA benchmarks and NQ/HotpotQA training coverage, while adding MATH500 mathematical reasoning with Python execution and WebDetective long-horizon deep search. These introduce substantially different task requirements beyond the original short-answer QA evaluations.

E2.justification: The original Table 1 comparator set is unchanged. New comparisons add ZeroTIR-7B and SimpleTIR-7B on MATH500, and GPT-5-Chat, Gemini-2.5-Pro, and DeepSeek-V3.1 alongside Search-R1-3B-Base on WebDetective. This broadens comparisons to tool-reasoning and frontier models; Table 3 explicitly attributes frontier scores to the benchmark paper.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce Python tool execution and WebDetective's Pass@1 plus six search, generation, and knowledge-use metrics, substantially extending evaluation beyond QA exact match. Training-cost analysis also introduces non-IG runtime as an outcome-only proxy. Existing QA split descriptions and training hyperparameters remain unchanged; detailed protocols for the added benchmarks are limited.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 and Table 7 extend the qualitative training-overhead discussion into a component-level timing analysis, estimating a 1.9-fold slowdown using non-IG runtime as a proxy. Existing coefficient, sample-size, and search-turn analyses, training dynamics, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The bootstrap subsampling study using a 64-sequence reference and the existing plotted variability are unchanged. v3 adds no benchmark-level repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds MATH500 scores of 85.8% for InfoReasoner, 80.2% for ZeroTIR, and 84.6% for SimpleTIR; WebDetective Pass@1 is 30.0% versus Search-R1's 26.5%, although Forget is worse at 0.506 versus 0.483. Training-cost results are also new. Existing QA, ablation, and search-turn values are unchanged; these additions are not performance improvements over v1 under retained settings.

T1.justification: The POMDP definitions, assumptions, propositions, and appendix proofs are retained. Expressing the existing Equation (17) through negative log gold-class probability is an algebraic restatement. Revised discussion qualifies the connection to practical training without introducing a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the claimed empirical scope to mathematical tool use and long-horizon search, and describe the reward more explicitly as anchored to correctness. The central InfoReasoner contribution, theoretical properties, and original QA superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains that entropy reduction can reward confidently wrong answers and distinguishes that quantity from the supervised gold-class reward. Sections 2.3–2.4 qualify the practical implications of ideal telescoping gains. Existing failure cases and limitations largely remain, including some appendix prose that still conflates the two quantities.

D1.justification: v3 documents the backbones used for the added benchmarks and supplies hardware memory capacity, component timings, 39.35 hours of training, and 314.8 GPU-hours. These extend reproducibility information without establishing changed training settings. Existing hyperparameters, prompts, and retrieval-backend descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds substantive distinctions from IGPO's surface-form probability reward and EMPO's unsupervised semantic-entropy objective. References supporting the new benchmarks and baselines are also added. The existing survey is largely retained; IGPO and EMPO are discussed rather than experimentally compared.

P1.justification: The main narrative is reorganized: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Appendix A, the impact statement moves into the main text, and acknowledgements are added. The abstract, introduction, and theory-to-reward explanations are revised throughout to distinguish entropy reduction from the training reward.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from single-column to two-column layout, substantially reflowing figures, equations, tables, and case-study boxes. Three tables are added for WebDetective, MATH500, and training costs. Existing plot images are unchanged, although their sizes and arrangements change, including stacked Figure 4 panels.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency by distinguishing the gold-class training reward from entropy reduction and quantifying previously unspecified training overhead. MATH500 and WebDetective results broaden empirical support. The improvement is limited by sparse protocols and uncertainty reporting for the new comparisons, and by retained appendix language that leaves the theory-to-reward clarification incomplete.
